H1.quote: R-4 | Checkout and check-in work offline and sync when the phone is back online.

H2.quote: Personal data stays on the club's own hardware; no third-party cloud.

H3.quote: Runs on the club's existing Synology NAS with Docker, at 0 EUR per month.

H4.quote: R-6 | The kit manager receives an e-mail every Monday morning listing overdue kit.

H5.quote: QS-2 ... a coach scans the QR code on a kit bag and checks it out ... at most 3 taps and under 15 seconds from the scan

H6.quote: The treasurer exports a yearly inventory of kit as CSV for the insurance audit.

H7.quote: About 40 coaches and about 300 items. / Ruled out by the architect: performance efficiency ("performance is not a concern"), so no goal.

H8.quote: Written in Python: the only maintainer knows only Python, and a successor must be able to take over.

H9.quote: R-7 | Lost-item history is kept for 2 years, with the coach pseudonymised.

H10.quote: The kit manager is warned 30 days before the expiry date of a first-aid bag item.

H11.quote: Money handling: no deposits, fines or payments.

H12.quote: Must be live for the start of the season on 1 March.

unasked_decisions: The expiry warning is recorded as 'a notification inside the e-mail channel fixed by R-6'. The architect never said the expiry warning goes by the Monday e-mail. The channel was also still open, not 'fixed'.
The kit manager is recorded as 'the architect of this document'. This was assumed, never confirmed.
QG-4 is traced to R-6 and R-7 as well as R-5. This mapping was the designer's own and was never confirmed.
The club committee is kept as a stakeholder with 'no requirement of its own'. The architect only said they had 'no view' on it.
extras: Measured quality scenarios QS-1..QS-5: 95% spot-check match, 0 coach records readable without sign-in, every offline checkout appears after sync, a tested change in one day
Pseudonymisation of the coach in the 2-year lost-item history
No coach phone numbers in the Monday report
Phones keep as little personal data as possible (R-4 vs R-5 balance)
ADR 0001 lists the centrally decided topics: storage, sync and conflict rules, CSV format and versioning, report channel, dependencies
Treasurer, maintainer and successor added as stakeholders
Out of scope: player data, match results, membership system
Gaps: the confirmed 7-day overdue threshold, the coach-data retention rule (delete on leaving the club) and the R-4/R-5 risk entry were agreed but not written into the files
artifact: arc42.md (sections 1-3, 9 and 10 filled: an 8-row ranked R-list, QG-1..5, stakeholders, 4 constraints, scope, QS table), ADR 0001 (proposed), and two feature issues in .scratch/ (expiry warning, CSV export). The architect's final answers (approval, retention, risk) are not yet reflected.
